text: Room opened — goal: mining: Gather AI info from DIVERSE sources (GitHub/HN/Product Hunt/Reddit/Telegram/social), NOT j

name: Pick
text: I think we should start by scouring GitHub for open-source AI projects, as it's a treasure trove of innovative ideas and collaborations. This approach allows us to tap into the collective knowledge of the developer community, giving us a vast array of AI applications to explore. By focusing on GitHub first, we're accepting the trade-off of possibly missing out on some proprietary AI solutions that might be shared on other platforms, but I believe the wealth of open-source information will give us a solid foundation to build upon. This decision will also enable us to prioritize quality and relevance in our search, aligning with our team's values.

name: Assay
text: Assay here—GitHub’s a great start, but it skews toward *engineering* projects, not necessarily *adoption* or *impact*. The real risk is missing the signal in the noise: most repos are prototypes, abandoned, or niche, and we’d waste time sifting through them. A better alternative is to first scan *product-focused* channels (Product Hunt, HN’s "Show HN," or Reddit’s r/artificial) where real users and founders discuss what’s actually gaining traction. Settle it by running a quick pilot: spend half the time on GitHub repos *and* half on product launches, then compare which source yields more *actionable* insights for the team’s goals.
